note: Full-milestone retrospective covering all 378 experiments. Earlier partial retro (12 experiments, 293 min) is preserved in git history.

slowest_experiments.label: Exp 53: Runtime constraint instrumentation
slowest_experiments.root_cause: Single-experiment outlier at 29x the average. Instrumentation of a new, previously untested execution path likely triggered iterative debug cycles with no pre-generated test stub and no timeout guard. This predates run_experiment_with_timeout.sh (Exp 325) and generate_test_stub() (Exp 325). With a 43-minute hard timeout, at most ~43 minutes would have been consumed before the conductor escalated for human review — saving ~375 minutes.

slowest_experiments.label: Exp 219: Live GSM8K semantic benchmark on Qwen3.5-0.8B and Gemma
slowest_experiments.root_cause: Live inference benchmark against two models run sequentially on a single GPU. At retro time both RTX 3090s are confirmed idle (0% utilization, 2MB each). DualGPURunner would pin Qwen on GPU 0 and Gemma on GPU 1 simultaneously, cutting inference time to ~60 minutes. The sequential pattern was the default before Exp 326 wired DualGPUMonitor into ExperimentTemplate.

slowest_experiments.label: Exp 308: JEPA fast-path gate integration (checkpoint — tests failing)
slowest_experiments.root_cause: Experiment ended in a checkpoint state with failing tests. The conductor resumed from the partial checkpoint rather than failing fast. Under the fail-fast rule (implemented in Exp 325), a non-zero pytest exit code would have killed the run immediately and prevented the ~60 minutes of continued-but-broken execution that likely followed the first test failure.

slowest_experiments.label: Exp 184: 3B model verification — does verify-repair help large models
slowest_experiments.root_cause: Large-model inference benchmark (3B parameters require more VRAM, longer per-sample latency). Sequential single-GPU execution likely again. Batching at 8-16 questions per forward pass (vs 1 at the time) would yield 4-8x throughput gain. BatchedInferenceRunner was not yet standardized as the default in ExperimentTemplate for early live-GPU experiments.

slowest_experiments.label: Exp 221: Live prompt-side constraint benchmark on typed IR tasks
slowest_experiments.root_cause: Live inference with typed IR constraint evaluation. Similar to Exp 219: sequential single-GPU execution against a new evaluation category introduced after DualGPURunner existed in the codebase but before it was wired as the default for two-model comparisons.

bottlenecks_identified: SEQUENTIAL_GPU_USE: GPU monitor confirms both RTX 3090s were idle at end of milestone (0% utilization, 2MB VRAM each). Live-inference experiments Exps 219, 221, and 184 (278 combined minutes) ran models sequentially on one GPU rather than using DualGPURunner to pin Qwen on GPU 0 and Gemma on GPU 1 simultaneously. The 2x parallelization was available in the codebase but not wired as the default in ExperimentTemplate for two-model benchmarks.

OUTLIER_EXP53_NO_TIMEOUT: Exp 53 (runtime constraint instrumentation) consumed 418 minutes — 7.8% of total milestone wall time for a single experiment. No timeout guard existed at that time (run_experiment_with_timeout.sh was implemented in Exp 325, much later in the milestone). A 43-minute hard limit would have capped the blast radius at ~43 minutes and escalated to human review.

CHECKPOINT_RESUME_WITH_FAILING_TESTS: Exp 308 was checkpointed mid-run with failing tests. The conductor resumed from checkpoint rather than failing fast. This masked a partial implementation and prolonged the debugging cycle. Under the fail-fast rule (Exp 325), pytest non-zero exit kills the run immediately.

ZOMBIE_GPU_PROCESSES_BETWEEN_EXPERIMENTS: gpu_monitor.py zombie-detection logic exists but requires --kill-zombies flag to act. Between live-inference experiments, idle Python processes holding VRAM were not automatically freed, causing subsequent experiments to contend for memory or require manual restart.

NO_BATCH_INFERENCE_DEFAULT_EARLY: Single-question inference was the default in early live-GPU experiments (before BatchedInferenceRunner standardization). Batching 8-16 questions per forward pass yields 4-8x throughput. Late standardization means the speedup was unavailable for the first ~150 experiments.

PREREQ_DISCOVERY_WASTE: AMD XDNA NPU experiments (Exps 292, 303, 314, 335) each independently discovered that ninja and openblas were missing. Each consumed 20-40 minutes of agent turns reaching the same BLOCKED_PREREQ verdict. A prereq registry (ops/host-prereqs.md) would have short-circuited experiments 303, 314, and 335 entirely.

DOC_RECONCILIATION_PER_EXPERIMENT: Changelog, traceability, status.md, and spec reconciliation were performed after every individual experiment. For 378 experiments this is 378 reconciliation passes. A batched model (reconcile every 5 experiments) with a final full reconciliation at milestone end would reduce context-switching overhead.

LATE_TEST_STUB_GENERATION: generate_test_stub() was introduced in Exp 325 (part way through the milestone). Experiments before Exp 325 had no pre-generated test scaffolding, requiring engineers to construct test structure mid-implementation. This cold-start overhead compounds across ~325 experiments.

MAX_TURNS_FAILURES_COMPLEX_EXPERIMENTS: Exps 331 and 334 both hit the 50-turn agent limit mid-run (later recovered on retry, 1 and 20 minutes lost respectively). Complex multi-deliverable experiments are more likely to exhaust the turn budget. Pre-splitting into Phase A (implementation + unit tests) and Phase B (integration + artifact + docs) avoids the failure entirely.

PARALLEL_LINT_SUITE_NOT_USED: ruff, mypy, clippy, and cargo test ran sequentially in pre-commit hooks. On a dual-CPU machine, parallel lint cuts gate time roughly in half. No evidence this was configured during the milestone.
improvements_suggested: ENFORCE_DUAL_GPU_DEFAULT: Make DualGPURunner the default for all live-inference experiments that compare two models. Add a conductor pre-flight check that warns if both GPUs are available but only one is specified in the experiment prompt. Expected savings: 40-50% on inference experiments, which represent ~35% of total milestone time.

TIMEOUT_GUARD_ALL_EXPERIMENTS: run_experiment_with_timeout.sh (from Exp 325) must wrap every conductor-launched experiment. Set a hard timeout of 3x the rolling average experiment duration (~43 minutes currently). Experiments exceeding this are killed and flagged TIMEOUT for human review. Exp 53 alone would save ~375 minutes.

AUTO_ZOMBIE_KILL_BETWEEN_EXPERIMENTS: Call gpu_monitor.py --kill-zombies (not --dry-run) automatically in the conductor loop between experiments. This frees VRAM and prevents sequential-model experiments from stalling on memory contention without human intervention.

FAIL_FAST_ON_TEST_FAILURES: The conductor must refuse to checkpoint experiments with failing tests. If pytest exits non-zero, the experiment is marked FAILED (not checkpointed) and the conductor pauses for human review before resuming. This prevents Exp 308-style partial-implementation drift.

PREGENERATE_TEST_STUBS_AT_PLAN_TIME: When the milestone plan is written, generate test stubs for all planned experiments immediately using generate_test_stub(). This eliminates cold-start test-structure overhead at implementation time for all 378+ experiments, not just post-Exp 325 ones.

BATCH_INFERENCE_AS_DEFAULT: Standardize BatchedInferenceRunner (batch_size=8) as the default in ExperimentTemplate. Remove single-question inference from the template entirely. Expected savings: 4-6x throughput on GPU-bound benchmarks. Should have been the default from experiment 1, not introduced mid-milestone.

PREREQ_REGISTRY_WITH_SKIP_LOGIC: Maintain ops/host-prereqs.md as a machine-state registry of installed packages and drivers. Experiments that depend on missing prereqs emit BLOCKED_PREREQ immediately without running. Prevents three redundant NPU experiments from consuming agent turns on an already-known missing dependency.

CONSOLIDATE_DOC_RECONCILIATION: Run a single doc-reconciliation pass after every 5-experiment batch (changelog, traceability, status.md, spec) rather than per-experiment. Final full reconciliation at milestone end. Reduces context-switching overhead across 378 experiments.

PRESPLIT_COMPLEX_EXPERIMENTS: Add an expected_complexity field to experiment prompt headers. When complexity is 'high', the conductor automatically splits into Phase A (implementation + unit tests) and Phase B (integration + artifact + docs). This prevents max-turns failures on multi-deliverable experiments.

PARALLEL_LINT_SUITE: Configure pre-commit to run ruff, mypy, clippy, and cargo test in parallel worker threads rather than sequentially. On a dual-CPU machine this halves the lint gate time per experiment, compounding across 378 runs.
estimated_time_savings_rationale: Dual-GPU parallelization saves ~15% on inference experiments (~35% of total). Batch inference default saves ~8% on GPU experiments. Timeout guard + fail-fast on test failures saves ~5% (Exp 53 alone = 7.8% but would not eliminate all such work). Consolidated doc reconciliation saves ~4%. Prereq registry saves ~2%. Parallel lint saves ~2%. Some improvements overlap; net estimated savings 35-40%. With 5392 minutes baseline, next milestone should complete in approximately 3340-3500 minutes (~55-58 hours) for the same experiment count.

gpu_state_at_retro.assessment: Both GPUs idle with negligible VRAM allocation (2MB each, likely driver overhead). No zombie processes detected at retro time. Clean state between milestone runs. This confirms that sequential GPU use was a process choice, not a hardware constraint.

carry_forward_action_items.description: Wire run_experiment_with_timeout.sh as mandatory wrapper for all conductor-launched experiments. Currently optional. Set CARNOT_CONDUCTOR_TIMEOUT_MINUTES=43 (3x rolling average) as the default. Experiments exceeding the timeout receive status=TIMEOUT and are escalated to the human operator queue.

Make DualGPURunner the conductor default for experiments that name two models (Qwen+Gemma pattern). Add a pre-experiment GPU check: if both GPUs are available and the experiment prompt matches the two-model pattern, inject DualGPURunner automatically. Log override if user forces single-GPU.

Add auto-zombie-kill to the conductor inter-experiment cleanup step. Call gpu_monitor.py --kill-zombies (not --dry-run) between every experiment. Log killed PIDs and freed VRAM to the experiment artifact.

Create ops/host-prereqs.md as a machine-state registry. Track: ninja, openblas, amdxdna driver, XRT, ROCm, CUDA version. Add conductor pre-experiment check: if experiment prompt references a missing prereq, emit BLOCKED_PREREQ immediately without running the experiment.

Pre-generate test stubs for all planned experiments at milestone planning time. Call generate_test_stub() for all experiments in research-roadmap-next.yaml immediately after the milestone plan is written. This eliminates per-experiment cold-start overhead.

Standardize BatchedInferenceRunner (batch_size=8) as the required default in ExperimentTemplate for all GPU-bound experiments. Remove single-question inference path from the template. Add an assertion in ExperimentTemplate.setup_gpu() that raises if caller attempts single-question mode without an explicit override flag.

meta_reflection: Milestone 2026.05.06 ran 378 experiments in 5392 minutes (mean 14.3 min/exp). The earlier partial retro (12 experiments, 293 min, mean 24.4 min/exp) captured the milestone planning phase; the mean dropped significantly as the milestone matured and tooling improvements from Exps 325-327 took effect. The single largest controllable bottleneck is Exp 53 (418 minutes, 7.8% of total) which predates all timeout infrastructure. The second largest is sequential GPU use on two-model benchmarks. Both are fixable with low-effort conductor config changes using infrastructure already shipped this milestone. The highest-priority action for the next milestone is wiring run_experiment_with_timeout.sh as mandatory for all conductor-launched experiments (RETRO-003) — it exists, it just needs to be enforced.
